Subject: On-prem / Air-gapped qualification - hardware & offline ops follow-up

Thanks again for taking the call today, John - really helpful to understand the constraints at Legacy. Per our discussion I wanted to summarize the open items we agreed to validate for an air-gapped on-prem deployment and propose next steps.

Summary of requirements from call:
- Environment: fully air-gapped, no outbound internet egress from inference nodes; control plane via private peering/VPN only
- Hardware: prefer to confirm exact GPU models and NVMe sizing; you mentioned current cluster is NVIDIA A100-80GB but some sites have A10s
- Upgrades/maintenance: must be able to perform offline upgrades with a maintenance window and rollback plan; prefer in-place kernelless upgrades if possible
- KMS/keys: bring-your-own KMS (on-prem HSM) required for key management; audit log retention 7 years
- Networking: no public DNS resolution from nodes, whitelisting only for management bastion; separate management plane for staging

Actions I'm taking:
- Attach: Redwood on-prem hardware checklist (initial) - Marissa to validate against your rack/hardware inventory
- Schedule: technical deep dive with Stephanie (solutions engineering) to map GPU footprint and offline upgrade flow

Requested from Legacy (please send if available):
- Current hardware inventory (GPU model, CPU, RAM, NVMe sizes) per rack/site
- Network diagram for the management plane and bastion host (what can remain reachable)
- Preferred maintenance windows and on-call escalation path

Next step proposals:
1) John/IT Ops: share HW inventory + management network diagram by Mon 2027-05-03
2) Redwood: set up 60-minute technical session week of 2027-05-10 to confirm upgrade process and offline installation playbook

Thanks - I'll follow up with a calendar invite once I hear availability.

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear notes. Attaching the network diagram and our current inventory export (redacted) - see attached. A few clarifications:

- Hardware: most inference racks are A100-80GB but we have two older A10 racks that are candidates for decommissioning in Q3. For the A100 racks we have 2 x 2U chassis with 8 GPUs each, Mellanox CX6 networking.
- Storage: NVMe per node is 4TB; we plan to increase to 8TB for model shards if needed.
- Maintenance: offline upgrades are doable but must be coordinated; we prefer rolling upgrades by rack with a max 2 hour per-rack maintenance window.
- KMS: we have an on-prem HSM (Luna) and can provision key material to the Redwood control plane via an HSM export process that has to be completed on our side.

Quick Qs for Redwood: 
1) Does Redwood support a fully offline installer that can be executed via air-gapped USB media and a management bastion?
2) What are the GPU memory requirements / recommended shard sizes for the model you demoed (redwood-llm-3B variant)?

Appreciate the inventory and network diagram, John - that's perfect. Answering your questions and next steps below.

1) Offline installer: Yes - Redwood provides an air-gapped installer flow. The standard path is:
   - We provide a signed installation bundle (tarball) and a verification manifest.
   - Customer downloads bundle to an isolated management workstation (via secure transfer) and transfers to the bastion/air-gapped staging host via encrypted media.
   - Installer executes and performs a local package install and config apply; control plane connection is established via the pre-provisioned VPN/peering when available.
   - We also provide an offline health check utility for pre- and post-install validation.

2) GPU memory / shard sizing: Stephanie - feel free to add exact numbers below, but as a baseline for the redwood-llm-3B variant we recommend 40-60GB of GPU memory for a single-replica low-latency configuration; with model sharding you can run on 4 x A10/A100 combination (depending on perf targets).

Proposed next steps:
- Schedule 60-minute technical session: Thu 2027-05-13 11:00-12:00 PT (I'll send invite, please confirm)
- Procurement: once tech session validates SOW we'll issue a draft SOW and an initial BOM for hardware/installation services


Marissa

Thanks - adding technical notes from my side before the call:

- Model footprint: For production latency SLOs we target 0.2-0.4s per token on A100-80GB for the redwood-llm-3B variant with 16 beam cache and continuous batching. Expect lower perf on A10; we can provide quantized variants to reduce memory footprint.
- NVMe: 8TB is a safe target if you plan to host sharded model checkpoints locally; if you prefer more aggressive caching we can do 4TB + remote NFS for checkpoints during initial seeding (but NFS requires management plane access).
- Offline upgrades: Our upgrade package supports precomputed kernel modules and a staged rollback that preserves KV cache snapshots; during the tech call I'll walk through the playbook and a sample runbook we use with other regulated customers.

I'll prepare a short deck and a runbook snippet to share in the call. If you can confirm which racks are A100 vs A10 in the inventory we can map an upgrade order that minimizes risk.


Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
